hypothesis: H4: an OUTLINED bead cell (abs(cellD-gRingGap)) is more legible than a SOLID one (cellD-gRingGap)
why: OUTLINED wins decisively on LATTICE legibility and loses on BEAD-NAMING. Mechanism is compositing, not exposure: fractal() accumulates front-to-back as w=(1-alpha)*f, so a coverage f that saturates over a whole cell interior drives alpha->1 on the COARSEST drawn level and OCCLUDES all 5 deeper levels. Solid therefore renders exactly ONE scale - measured edge energy drops 36-61% (kiku .033->.021, tomoe .050->.019, ume .043->.021) while mean luminance TRIPLES. Polarity also inverts: glowing line on black becomes black seam on a pastel ground, which kills the 'glowing filament in the dark' read the mon were chosen for. Solid's one genuine win is that the silhouette becomes nameable at a single scale.

luminance.method: mean Rec709 luma of the canvas, 256x256 downsample, noaudio, time ladder t=4/8/16, 880x750 viewport

counter_ratchet: TWO DIFFERENT ANSWERS, do not conflate. (a) BEAD_MIX hex->bead: NO blanket counter-ratchet. Effect is small and motif-dependent with varying SIGN - kiku -1%, tomoe +1%, ume +10% - so a blanket compensation would over-brighten ume. Confirms and extends the tomoe teammate's 12.20->12.71 finding. (b) SOLID_MIX outlined->solid: counter-ratchet REQUIRED and it can be a CONSTANT - 3.3-3.9x on all three motifs, motif-independent. Implemented as SOLID_FIX (knob_162, default off in this scratch file): keep level COVERAGE f on the ring distance so solid cannot occlude the recursion, and route SOLID_MIX only into the FILL distance, then scale the fill term by fillW=0.30. Lands solid at 0.068-0.072 vs outlined 0.056-0.066 and restores multi-level depth while keeping solid cell bodies. Nothing touches the global multiplier (K160).
refutes: Coordinator prediction that the outlined-vs-solid answer swings with boundary crossings per ray. It does NOT. Low-crossing tomoe (~1) and high-crossing kiku (12) / ume (5+notches) collapse IDENTICALLY under solid, because the collapse is front-to-back occlusion and any saturated interior causes it regardless of silhouette topology. Crossing count strongly changes the OUTLINED arm only - ume outlined was the most striking cell tested, agreeing with the keeper-candidate call.
next: Ship SOLID_FIX as the real variant-2 knob: it is a third arm (solid bodies + preserved recursion) that neither pure arm gives. Then re-test bead-naming vs lattice-depth on that arm.
